subject: GPU Mosaic Sizing & Fallback Playbook — RFI response
messages:

Cc: ops-team@novaai.com
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: sizing guidance for 'Mosaic' production inference (heterogeneous GPU mix)

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking this RFI. We're scoping a pilot for our Mosaic product (multimodal LLM + reranker) and need detailed guidance for committed reserved capacity. Our key constraints:
- Peak concurrent requests: ~3,200 req/s (short sequences) and 700 req/s (longer sequences, up to 4k tokens) depending on endpoint.
- P95 latency SLO per endpoint: 150ms (short), 450ms (long).
- Cold-start tolerance: < 500ms additional for pre-warmed pool.
- Cost target: unit token cost <= $0.0009 where possible.

Questions in the RFI (attached): preferred GPU blends, quantization tradeoffs, pre-warm pool sizing, slotting/fallback rules when capacity constrained, and operational recommendations for canary/failover.

Please respond with a recommended reserve plan (GPU families & counts), fallback model variants, and a workbook with throughput projections. If possible, include a worked example for a mixed workload (60% short, 40% long).

We'd like a first draft by EOD Thursday, 24 Jun.

Best,
Sarah
Director, Platform Ops
NovaAI

Attachment: mosaic-rfi-template.pdf
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: sizing guidance for 'Mosaic' production inference (heterogeneous GPU mix)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and the template. Attached is an initial workbook and a short playbook describing the heterogeneous (mosaic) approach we've seen work for similar mixed-token workloads. Summary highlights (full detail in workbook):

- Recommended reserved GPU blend (pilot): 8x H100-80GB, 12x A100-80GB, 16x L4-48GB as a mix to serve high-throughput short requests on L4, heavy long requests on H100, with A100 as general-purpose mid-latency capacity.
- Quantization: use 4-bit (GPTQ or AWQ) for short/embedding-heavy routes; 8-bit-float for long-sequence generation where quality loss is sensitive.
- Slotting: map endpoints to logical slot types (short/fast, long/throughput, regen), and reserve a 10% burst lane for pre-warmed handoffs.
- Fallback policy: when H100 capacity is saturated, route to A100 with reduced max-length and an automatic response explaining degraded mode (policy + telemetry).
- Pre-warm pool sizing heuristic: pre-warm = max(4% of reserved pool, enough to sustain 300 concurrent short requests) — reduces cold-start tails.

I've attached: mosaic-sizing-workbook-v1.xlsx and latency-sla-matrix.pdf. Workbook includes a mixed-workload projection (60/40 short/long) and cost sensitivity tabs.

We'll hold a short call Wednesday 23 Jun at 10am PT if that works to walk the workbook.

Regards,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

1) For long requests that get routed to A100 as fallback, what is the expected latency uplift percentage (P50/P95)?
2) Your pre-warm heuristic references "300 concurrent short requests" — can you show the math tied to L4 per-GPU concurrency assumptions?

If you can include a worked example in the workbook showing throttling behavior at 95% reserved utilization that'd be helpful.

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: RFI: sizing guidance for 'Mosaic' — clarifications from NovaAI (two asks)

Folks — NovaOps asked for: (1) expected latency uplift when routing long requests to A100 as fallback, and (2) show L4 math for pre-warm sizing. I sketched answers below; please review and update before the 10am call with them.

Quick sketch (please correct):
- Assumptions: short request avg tokens=64, long avg tokens=2,400, model baseline is open-multimodal-13B quantized where short route uses 4-bit and long route uses 8-bit-float.
- L4 concurrency: we can sustain ~160 short-generation QPS per L4 with 16-token context windows using batching; conservative pre-warm concurrency = 120 per L4 for tail safety.
- Pre-warm pool: to sustain 300 concurrent short requests at 120 concurrency/GPU => need 3 GPUs pre-warmed => round up to 4 for cushion and host overhead.
- A100 fallback uplift: from H100 P95 420ms (long) to A100 P95 ~560ms => ~33% uplift under comparable batching; P50 uplift smaller (~15–20%). These numbers assume similar batch packing and KV cache locality.

Questions for you both: are we comfortable with 160 QPS/L4 (conservative) and the A100 uplift numbers? Also propose we include a canary policy: keep 2 H100 slots on warm standby during initial 30-day ramp.

Thanks — jasmine
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI: sizing guidance for 'Mosaic' — clarifications from NovaAI (two asks)

Jasmine/Marcus — looks good. A few technical clarifications to fold into the workbook before the call:

1) L4 per-GPU sustained short-route concurrency: 140 QPS realistic if we apply continuous batching and 256-token packing windows; 120 is fine for conservative pre-warm. I'll add a microbench summary to the workbook.

2) A100 fallback uplift: +25–35% at P95 depending on batch packing. Add a regression corridor in the workbook: optimistic +20%, median +30%, pessimistic +40% for stress runs.

3) Slotting: propose these logical slot counts for the pilot (targeting 95% utilization headroom planning):
- Short/fast slots (L4): 70 slots mapped to 16 L4 GPUs (allowing 4 slots spare for pre-warm).
- Mid/general slots (A100): 40 slots mapped to 12 A100 GPUs.
- Long/high-memory slots (H100): 14 slots mapped to 8 H100 GPUs (with 2 reserved warm standby).

I'll update the mosaic-sizing-workbook-v1.xlsx with these numbers and include a stress sheet for 95% reserved utilization and the automatic fallback telemetry fields we recommend.

-karthik

Subject: Re: RFI: sizing guidance for 'Mosaic' production inference — finalized pilot playbook and next steps

Sarah — thank you for the questions and the call. Attached is mosaic-sizing-workbook-v1.xlsx (updated) with the worked example, microbench notes, and a stress sheet showing behavior at 95% reserved utilization. Highlights and next steps: 

- Pilot reserve recommendation: 16 L4 (short/fast), 12 A100 (general), 8 H100 (long/high-memory) — aligns with the workbook slot mapping.
- Quantization baseline: short endpoints => AWQ/4-bit, long endpoints => Q8/8-bit-float. Quality regression risk flagged for a small subset of generation prompts (noted in workbook).
- Fallback policy: A100 fallback with automatic max_length reduction and a telemetry-flagged response. Uplift corridor: P95 +20/+30/+40% (opt/median/worst) included.
- Pre-warm pool: maintain 4 pre-warmed L4 instances for cold-start reduction (math shown in workbook).
- Canary & ramp: keep 2 H100 warm-standby GPUs for first 30 days; run A/B traffic split 95/5 for canary rollout.

Requesting: please confirm by EOD Friday 02 Jul if NovaAI wants Redwood to propose a reserved pricing commitment based on the pilot blend. If yes, we'll produce a price/term proposal and a DocuSign scope-of-work.

Thanks — looking forward to working together.

Best,
Jasmine Liu

Redwood Inference
